    Closed words give infinitely many indecomposables #

    A primitive band without zero paths gives the indecomposable, pairwise non-isomorphic band modules M(b, t), t ∈ kˣ (not_isRepFinite_of_band). Over a gentle algebra, a closed word with all cyclic adjacent pairs allowed has a primitive root which is such a band (not_isRepFinite_of_closed, Theorem 4.5, band part).

    theorem BrickAccessibility.CWord.follow_facts {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {D : MonomialData k B} (S : D.Signs) (b : CWord D.Q) (hA : Alt S b) (hall : ∀ (q : Fin b.n), D.AllowedPair (b.lt q) (b.lt (b.succ q))) (l : List D.Q.A) (i j : Fin b.n) :
    b.followPos i l = some j → D.Q.IsWalk (b.vtx i) (List.map (fun (x : D.Q.A) => (x, true)) l) ∧ ∀ (m : ℕ) (hm : m + 1 < l.length), D.pval (D.Q.src l[m]) [l[m], l[m + 1]] ≠ 0

    A primitive band without zero paths makes the algebra representation-infinite.

    source
    theorem BrickAccessibility.CWord.exists_prim_band {k : Type u} [Field k] {B : Type u} [Ring B] [Algebra k B] {D : MonomialData k B} (S : D.Signs) {v : D.Q.V} {s : Bool} {f : ℕ → Letter D.Q} (hv : S.Valid v s (HWord.inf f)) {L : ℕ} (hL : 0 < L) (hperL : ∀ (m : ℕ), f (m + L) = f m) :
    ∃ (b : CWord D.Q) (_ : Alt S b), (∀ (p q : Fin b.n), b.rightW p = b.rightW q → p = q) ∧ (∀ (q : Fin b.n), b.lt q = f ↑q) ∧ (∀ (q : Fin b.n), b.lt (b.succ q) = f (↑q + 1)) ∧ b.n ≤ L
